title: The Book of Knowledge
hookLine: the first book: foundations, character, study, idolatry and repentance

cards: A law code is a practical thing. You open it with a question in hand: may I carry this on Shabbat, is this pot still kosher, what do I owe the worker by sundown.
So you might expect Maimonides' code to start with something useful. A blessing over bread. The rules of the morning.
Instead, its first book is about what a person knows. Who God is. What a good character looks like.
Why study matters. What it means to worship something false. How to come back after doing wrong.

teach.h: BOOK. KNOWLEDGE. THE BOOK OF KNOWLEDGE.
teach.b: Sefer HaMadda. Sefer is book, madda is knowledge: the Book of Knowledge. First, what's inside.
Maimonides groups his code into books, and each book into sets of laws. This one holds the laws of the foundations of the Torah, of character, of Torah study, of idolatry, and of repentance.
Notice the path that list walks. Knowing God. Becoming a certain kind of person.
Learning. Guarding against false worship. Returning when you fall.
Second, the surprise. These are laws. He writes about knowing God and shaping your temper in the same plain, orderly style he uses elsewhere for damages and contracts.
To him, how you think and who you are fall under commandment as much as what you eat. Third, the order. He could have put this book anywhere.
The inner life comes first, and the outward life of blessings, festivals and courts is built on top of it.
Knowing comes before doing. Fourth, the last word.
The book ends with repentance, teshuvah. Before the reader meets a single rule about Shabbat or food, the code has already explained how to come back from failing.
Knowledge first, and a way home already built in.

how: Jews who study the Mishneh Torah often begin with the Book of Knowledge, and some study a set portion of the code each day, working through it in order.

games.q: you're writing a code of all Jewish law, for ordinary people. where do you put the laws about knowing God and shaping character?
o: at the very end, as an appendix.
at the very beginning, before everything else.
nowhere: a law code is for actions.
games.why: Maimonides put them first, in the Book of Knowledge. the inner life is the foundation, and the rest of the code is built on top of it.

practice: Here is the code's first line, in plain English: the foundation of foundations, and the pillar of all wisdom, is to know that there is a First Being.
Say it once in your head, and notice which word your mind catches on: foundation, pillar, know, or first. Don't explain it; just stay near that one word, and come back to it each time you drift.

wordCard.voice: Sefer HaMadda. The Book of Knowledge, the opening book of Maimonides' code, where foundations, character, study, idolatry and repentance come before everything else. Today's word.
